summary: The long rectangular gable-roof silhouette is recognizable, but the model reads as a brick utility hut rather than the russet shingle-clad studio in SV1. Principal-entry placement is plausible but not proven.

orientation.summary: The map and located SV1 look SSE toward the +v/NW gable and clearly establish that face as a blank end with an attic vent and low grille. The render agrees that +v has no door, while the actual inventory contains one principal-sized door only on the opposite -v/SE face. However, that opposite face is concealed in the supplied geolocated view, so no source directly confirms the entrance there; nearest-road relationships are not evidence.

issues.problem: Principal-entry orientation remains unresolved: the sole -v door is only an inference from the blank +v view.
issues.fix: Supply geolocated evidence of the -v end or another source that locates the principal entrance; otherwise mark its placement uncertain rather than approving it.

issues.problem: The walls use conspicuous brick texture, whereas SV1 shows russet-brown shingle/panel cladding, changing the building’s identity.
issues.fix: Replace the brick courses with simplified brown shingle courses or subtle rectangular panels.

issues.problem: The characteristic centered louvered attic vent on +v is modeled as a dark glazed-looking square; the roof also appears somewhat too steep and dominant.
issues.fix: Use a shallow, horizontally slatted vent and modestly reduce the gable pitch while retaining the long simple roof form and low grille.
